newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt policeman shot dead in Gaza border clash.
newsitem.headline: Egypt policeman shot dead in Gaza border clash.

text.p: An Egyptian police lieutenant was killed on Friday by Israeli attack helicopters that fired into the town of Rafah after an Israeli colonel was killed in a clash with Palestinians, security sources in Cairo said.

Witnesses in Rafah, located at the border between Gaza and Egypt, said the helicopters fired into the town after Israeli Colonel Nabi Mari was killed in a clash with Palestinian police and protestors.
Medical sources in Rafah said more than 40 Palestinians were wounded and that about 1,000 Arabs living close to the border fled their homes.
The Israeli army said Mari was killed and two soldiers were wounded after shots were fired from both the Gazan and Egyptian sides of the border.
"Israeli helicopters fired in the Palestinian area in order to help rescue the wounded from an Israeli outpost," the army said, insisting no shots were fired into Egypt.

Egyptian Lieutenant Motaz Fares Ashour is the second Egyptian officer to be killed in the border clashes. On Thursday, Major Muawwad Abdellatif Abu Galil was hit at the Rafah checkpoint on the Egyptian side, the sources said.
Under self-rule deals that launched Palestinian autonomy in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, Israel remained in control of the borders of the self-rule areas.

Seven Palestinians and three Israelis were killed in a third day of violence in the West Bank and Gaza Strip on Friday in the aftermath of Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy places in Jerusalem.
